test_cases.title: Deleting a book with an active borrowing is rejected by the foreign key constraint
preconditions: User is authenticated as ADMIN (admin user id 1 exists with role ADMIN).
Book id 1 exists in the catalog.
Book id 1 has exactly one active borrowing (borrowing id 1, status ACTIVE) by member user id 2.
Confirmation flag is set to confirm (the DELETE statement is issued).
constraints: borrowings.book_id references books.id with ON DELETE RESTRICT, so a book with borrowings cannot be deleted.
setup_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, username VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (char_length(username) BETWEEN 3 AND 50), email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL, role VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('ADMIN','MEMBER')))

CREATE TABLE books (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, author TEXT NOT NULL, isbn VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE, description TEXT, total_copies INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (total_copies > 0), available_copies INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (available_copies >= 0 AND available_copies <= total_copies), created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 00:00:00', updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 00:00:00')

CREATE TABLE borrowings (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), book_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES books(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, borrow_date DATE NOT NULL, due_date DATE NOT NULL, return_date DATE, status VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('ACTIVE','RETURNED')), CHECK (due_date >= borrow_date))
INSERT INTO users (id, username, email, password_hash, role) VALUES (1, 'admin_user', 'admin@library.org', 'hashed_admin_pw', 'ADMIN')
INSERT INTO users (id, username, email, password_hash, role) VALUES (2, 'member_one', 'member1@library.org', 'hashed_member_pw', 'MEMBER')
INSERT INTO books (id, title, author, isbn, description, total_copies, available_copies) VALUES (1, 'Database Systems', 'C. J. Date', '9780321197849', 'Intro to databases', 3, 2)
INSERT INTO borrowings (id, user_id, book_id, borrow_date, due_date, return_date, status) VALUES (1, 2, 1, DATE '2024-01-10', DATE '2024-02-09', NULL, 'ACTIVE')

verification_assertions.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM books WHERE id = 1
SELECT id, title, author, isbn, total_copies, available_copies FROM books WHERE id = 1
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM borrowings WHERE book_id = 1 AND status = 'ACTIVE'
SELECT id, user_id, book_id, status FROM borrowings WHERE id = 1

expected_outcome.assertion_description: The DELETE is rejected because borrowing id 1 still references book id 1; PostgreSQL raises a foreign key constraint violation. The book row and its active borrowing remain unchanged.

test_cases.title: Borrowing the last available copy sets available copies to 0 and creates a borrowing record
preconditions: Book id 1 exists with total_copies = 1 and available_copies = 1 (exactly one available copy).
Member user id 2 exists with role MEMBER, is authenticated, and has no active borrowings (within the borrowing limit).
The borrowings table is initially empty.
constraints: borrowings.book_id references books.id and borrowings.user_id references users.id.
Due date defaults to 30 days after the borrow date.
users.username and users.email are unique; books.isbn is unique.
setup_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, username VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (char_length(username) BETWEEN 3 AND 50), email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL, role VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('ADMIN','MEMBER')))

CREATE TABLE books (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, author TEXT NOT NULL, isbn VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE, description TEXT, total_copies INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (total_copies > 0), available_copies INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (available_copies >= 0 AND available_copies <= total_copies), created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 00:00:00', updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 00:00:00')

CREATE TABLE borrowings (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), book_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES books(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, borrow_date DATE NOT NULL, due_date DATE NOT NULL, return_date DATE, status VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('ACTIVE','RETURNED')), CHECK (due_date >= borrow_date))
INSERT INTO users (id, username, email, password_hash, role) VALUES (1, 'admin_user', 'admin@library.org', 'hashed_admin_pw', 'ADMIN')
INSERT INTO users (id, username, email, password_hash, role) VALUES (2, 'member_one', 'member1@library.org', 'hashed_member_pw', 'MEMBER')
INSERT INTO books (id, title, author, isbn, description, total_copies, available_copies) VALUES (1, 'The Last Copy', 'A. Writer', '9780000000011', 'Only one copy in stock', 1, 1)
test_cases.test_sql: INSERT INTO borrowings (id, user_id, book_id, borrow_date, due_date, return_date, status) VALUES (1, 2, 1, DATE '2024-03-01', DATE '2024-03-01' + INTERVAL '30 days', NULL, 'ACTIVE'); UPDATE books SET available_copies = available_copies - 1, updated_at = TIMESTAMP '2024-03-01 09:00:00' WHERE id = 1 AND available_copies > 0;

verification_assertions.query: SELECT available_copies FROM books WHERE id = 1
SELECT id, total_copies, available_copies FROM books WHERE id = 1
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM borrowings WHERE book_id = 1 AND user_id = 2 AND status = 'ACTIVE'
SELECT id, user_id, book_id, to_char(borrow_date, 'YYYY-MM-DD'), to_char(due_date, 'YYYY-MM-DD'), return_date, status FROM borrowings WHERE id = 1

expected_outcome.assertion_description: The borrowing succeeds: a new ACTIVE borrowing record (id 1) for member 2 and book 1 exists with due date 30 days after the borrow date, and the book's available_copies is decremented from 1 to 0, which satisfies the non-negative CHECK constraint.

test_cases.title: Successful book return increments available copies and marks borrowing as returned
preconditions: A member user exists (user_id = 1)
A book exists with total_copies = 3 and available_copies = 2 (one copy currently borrowed)
An active (BORROWED) borrowing record exists linking the member to the book with return_date NULL
setup_sql: CREATE TABLE users (user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, username VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (char_length(username) BETWEEN 3 AND 50), email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE, password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, role VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('ADMIN','MEMBER')))

CREATE TABLE books (book_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, author VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, isbn VARCHAR(20) UNIQUE, description TEXT, total_copies INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (total_copies > 0), available_copies INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (available_copies >= 0 AND available_copies <= total_copies), created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT '2024-01-01 00:00:00', updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT '2024-01-01 00:00:00')

CREATE TABLE borrowings (borrowing_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id), book_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES books(book_id), borrow_date DATE NOT NULL, due_date DATE NOT NULL, return_date DATE, status VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('BORROWED','RETURNED')), CHECK (due_date >= borrow_date), CHECK (return_date IS NULL OR return_date >= borrow_date))
INSERT INTO users (user_id, username, email, password_hash, role) VALUES (1, 'member01', 'member01@example.com', 'hashedpassword1', 'MEMBER')
INSERT INTO books (book_id, title, author, isbn, description, total_copies, available_copies) VALUES (10, 'Database Systems', 'Jane Doe', '9780000000010', 'Intro to DBMS', 3, 2)
INSERT INTO borrowings (borrowing_id, user_id, book_id, borrow_date, due_date, return_date, status) VALUES (100, 1, 10, '2024-03-01', '2024-03-31', NULL, 'BORROWED')
test_cases.test_sql: UPDATE borrowings SET status = 'RETURNED', return_date = DATE '2024-03-15' WHERE borrowing_id = 100 AND status = 'BORROWED'; UPDATE books SET available_copies = available_copies + 1, updated_at = TIMESTAMP '2024-03-15 10:00:00' WHERE book_id = 10;

verification_assertions.query: SELECT available_copies FROM books WHERE book_id = 10
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM books WHERE book_id = 10 AND available_copies >= 0 AND available_copies <= total_copies
SELECT status FROM borrowings WHERE borrowing_id = 100
SELECT borrowing_id, user_id, book_id, status, return_date::text FROM borrowings WHERE borrowing_id = 100
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM borrowings WHERE book_id = 10 AND status = 'BORROWED'

expected_outcome.assertion_description: After the return, the borrowing record status is RETURNED with return_date set, and the book's available_copies is incremented from 2 to 3, remaining a non-negative integer not exceeding total_copies.
